analysis: What changed versus Tuesday's 9:00 AM brief: the tape flipped from CPI-driven selling to a relief bounce, and the driver is AI-credit, not rates. CoreWeave beat Q3 revenue ($3.661B) and raised its 2026 outlook to $13.0-13.3B with an adjusted-profitability target of H1 2028, and the stock is +10.8% premarket; Nvidia is +4.23% premarket after a two-session wipeout of roughly $470-480B. But nothing about the rate problem changed: a December hike is still near 90% priced, the 10-year closed at 4.983% (+11.9 bps), and today the bond market is closed for Veterans Day, so equities trade the whole session without a fresh Treasury signal. Nvidia's bounce is technical relief after a five-session -16.4% slide, not resolution: the House reply deadline is today, no public reply has surfaced, a subpoena threat stands, and earnings land Nov 17 with the requested briefing Nov 18. The Anthropic IPO terms (S-1/A2 filed Nov 10, roadshow live, $70-78 range, up to ~$1.4T fully diluted, $26B private placement led by Google and Nvidia at ~$10B each) are the counterweight: the biggest AI names are literally underwriting the next AI listing even as the market questions AI spending. Signal vs noise: CoreWeave's raised outlook and profitability timeline are signal for the neocloud/AI-capex debate; Burry's 'heck of a trade' comment is color; the SpaceX Kessel rack report is single-source and peripheral; GoPro's delayed earnings are noise for this brief. The open's test is whether the Nasdaq's +1.68% futures lead holds without bonds to validate it.

community_signals.takeaway: Even as CoreWeave's stock rallies on the earnings beat and raised outlook, the HN discussion centers on the other side of the trade: the debt load funding the AI buildout, with the company's bond yield above 16% framed as AI credit stress. It is the credit-market counterpoint the equity bounce glosses over.
community_signals.title: CoreWeave bond yield tops 16% as AI credit stress rises

headlines.headline: Futures rebounded after Tuesday's hot-CPI slide: as of 5:18 AM ET, Nasdaq-100 futures +1.68%, S&P 500 futures +0.79%, Dow futures roughly flat (CNBC). Tuesday's close: S&P 500 7,520.93 (-0.38%), Nasdaq 25,065.88 (-0.74%), Dow 52,231.89 (-0.30%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A relief bounce led by tech futures after the market gave back part of Monday's surge — but the rate backdrop that caused Tuesday's slide has not changed.

headlines.headline: Nvidia +4.23% premarket to $176.04 as of 6:53 AM ET (Finnhub), after falling 4.27% Monday and 5.47% Tuesday to close at $168.89 — a two-session loss of roughly $470-480B in market value and a five-session slide of -16.4%. Today is the deadline for CEO Jensen Huang to reply to three House chairmen seeking a closed-door briefing (proposed Nov 18); no public reply had surfaced as of this morning, and Chairman Mast has threatened a subpoena. Michael Burry called the stock 'a heck of a trade' near-term while doubting its long-term moat. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17 (expected EPS $2.53, revenue $111.4B).
headlines.why_it_matters: Technical relief after the steepest governance-driven slide in years, but the stock is still trading the legal and congressional timeline, not the Nov 17 print — the House reply due today is the next catalyst.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave (CRWV) +10.8% premarket (CNBC, 5:08 AM ET) after Q3 revenue of $3,661M beat estimates and the company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $13.0-13.3B (vs $12.86B LSEG estimate), saying it expects to become profitable on an adjusted basis in the first half of 2028, easing debt-burden fears.
headlines.why_it_matters: The neocloud name was the epicenter of AI-spending and debt fears, so a beat plus a raised outlook and a profitability date is the single biggest sentiment input into the open — and it is lifting the whole AI complex with it.

headlines.headline: Anthropic filed Amendment No. 2 to its S-1 on Nov 10 and launched its IPO roadshow: 825M shares at $70-78, listing on Nasdaq as ANT, implying up to ~$1.4T fully diluted valuation. A concurrent $26B private placement includes about $10B each from Google and Nvidia, $2.5B from AMD, and $1B each from Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft. CNBC reports pricing expected Nov 18 and trading Nov 19 (dates not in the company's announcement, unconfirmed).
headlines.why_it_matters: The largest-ever IPO capital raise, and the megacaps in this brief are on the other side of it as buyers — a fresh, concrete AI-demand signal that cuts against the AI-spending-skepticism trade.

headlines.headline: October CPI rose 0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% expected) and core 0.3% (vs +0.2% expected) — the third straight 0.3% core reading. Traders price a December Fed hike as near-certain (~90%), with an 11.5% chance of a half-point move per CME FedWatch. The 10-year closed Tuesday at 4.983% (+11.9 bps); the bond market is closed today for Veterans Day, so there is no fresh Treasury read until Thursday.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rate reset is the overhang under the whole bounce: futures are up, but the hike repricing that sank Tuesday is intact and the 10-year is parked just under 5%.

headlines.headline: SpaceX (SPCX) +2.5% premarket after SemiAnalysis reported it is developing a custom AI rack, 'Kessel,' that would let it use Nvidia chips while choosing other hardware independently, for data centers and orbital computing. Wedbush's Dan Ives sees a 20-25% political discount on SpaceX shares and still expects a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla eventually, though with greater hurdles.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source report, so treat the Kessel detail as fragile — but the Ives comment matters for Tesla watchers: the SpaceX-Tesla deal thesis is still live, just harder.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight; units were $25.40 (-0.31%) at Tuesday midday. The only fresh angle is WTI rebounding to $86.53 premarket (+0.57%) after sliding to two-month lows, which steadies the energy backdrop. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. RBC raised its price target to $31 from $30 (Nov 7). Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September.
